apps.description:
30% off followed by another 20% off is not 50% off. Discount Stack calculates two successive percentage discounts on the remaining price, then adds optional tax to show an estimated amount to pay.

Save calculations with a name. Search your history, reopen an earlier calculation, adjust the values and calculate again. Change the app language, numeral style and currency independently. Changing currency does not convert exchange rates.

No account needed. Saved calculations stay on your device.
apps.name: Discount Stack

apps.description:
Turn work that would otherwise disappear into a record.

HaulStamp is a simple tool for tracking waiting time and cargo-handling time as the work happens.

When did the waiting begin?
How long did cargo handling take?
How many items were handled, and what was the weight per item?

Details that feel obvious in the moment can become hard to remember later. HaulStamp keeps them together as one record you can return to.

Review saved records anytime in History. If something needs correcting, you can edit it; the previous values, edit time, and reason for the change are kept in the record history.

Set separate hourly rates for waiting and cargo handling to see a reference amount based on the time you recorded.

Record quantity and weight per item to see the total weight.

Export and share records as PDF, CSV, or plain text.

Key features

- Track waiting time
- Track cargo-handling time
- Record quantity and weight per item
- See total weight
- Set separate hourly rates for waiting and cargo handling
- Calculate a reference amount from recorded time and hourly rates
- Review past records
- Edit records while keeping previous values, edit time, and reason
- Export as PDF, CSV, or text
- Switch among 55 interface languages

HaulStamp is not a large management system.

It is a small tool for keeping the work you did today in a form you can check again later.

Reference amounts are estimates based on the hourly rates you set and the time you record. They do not represent an invoice amount, unpaid amount, or legally recognized amount.

The initial release does not provide a way to delete saved records.
apps.name: HaulStamp

apps.description:
Knotless is a small app where you simply tap glowing knot tiles and watch them turn.

There are no rules.
No scores.
No ads.
No words on the screen.

Tap a tile, and the strand changes direction.
Tap again, and the colors shift.
The pattern feels like it is almost tangled, almost untangled, always moving.

Knotless is not an app for achieving anything.
It is just something to tap.
apps.name: Knotless

apps.description:
PromptDock AI is a lightweight prompt builder for people who repeatedly write similar AI prompts.

Choose a built-in template, fill in the fields, and generate a structured prompt in seconds. You can copy the result, open ChatGPT, save repeated input sets, restore prompt history, and create your own custom templates.

PromptDock AI is designed for indie developers, creators, app makers, and anyone who wants a faster, more reusable AI workflow.

Features:
- Built-in prompt templates
- Custom prompt templates
- Saved input sets
- Field suggestions
- Prompt history
- Favorite templates
- JSON export and import for custom templates
- One-tap copy
- Optional ChatGPT shortcut

Your data stays on your device. PromptDock AI does not require an account and does not collect personal information.
apps.name: PromptDock AI

apps.description:
ShopSuggest is an easy-to-enter, easy-to-edit shopping list app.

Create separate lists for multiple shops, or use it as a checklist for things around the home.

Drag items to reorder priorities at any time. Suggestions let you reuse previously entered items like templates, so frequently used items can be added again quickly. Progress tracking makes it easy to see what is already done.

Customise text, colours, icons, and strikethroughs to make each list easier to read.

There are no ads or in-app purchases. JSON export and import are available at any time for backup, transfer, or organising your data.
apps.name: ShopSuggest

apps.description:
Adding an item to reach free delivery? First see what happens to the full amount you pay.

Enter four amounts to compare your original basket with the basket after adding an item:
• Original cart subtotal
• Ordinary shipping fee
• Free-shipping threshold
• Extra item price

Check whether free delivery applies, compare the two totals and inspect the calculation. Only you can decide if the extra item is worth it.

Changing currency does not convert prices. All four amounts must be in the same currency.
Assumes the free-shipping threshold uses the entered cart subtotal. Tax, coupons, exclusions, other fees, refunds, and reward points are not inferred.
apps.name: Vekunel

apps.description:
How much can you still spend before checkout?

Cart Budget Calculator gives you one clear number while you shop: the amount left in your budget.

Set a shopping budget and add the prices of items as they enter your cart. The remaining amount updates so you can see whether the next item still fits.

Use it for groceries, household shopping, gifts, or any trip where you want a hard spending limit.

No bank connection. No expense history. No finance dashboard. Just the remaining shopping budget you need before you reach the register.
apps.name: Cart Budget Calculator

apps.description:
There was a time when my days were consumed by work and alcohol.

I would wake up with a heavy head and a bleak mood after drinking too much.
While wondering how to sober up, I would head back to work that seemed to have no end.

The project was a death march.
Every day, I repeated the same hell without knowing when it would end.

After work, I drank while stopping at convenience stores on my way home.
I had no time to play the games I once loved, and no room left to think about what I wanted.

My body and mind felt like mud.

Back then, there was a vending machine on the platform of my nearest station that sold canned shijimi clam miso soup.

When I drank it, I felt as though a little nourishment reached my clouded mind and restored a small amount of strength to keep living.

Just to drink that can of soup, I barely managed the 14-minute walk to the station.

It did not give me the power to change my life.
But I still had enough strength to go and drink that shijimi miso soup.

Looking back now, I think that was one small grain too.



Hitotsubu is an app for placing the small events and feelings of each day into a bottle, one grain at a time.

Something tasted good.
Something looked beautiful.
I laughed.
I felt relieved.
I finished something.
Someone helped me.
I somehow made it through today.

It does not have to be a major event.
You do not need an impressive goal or a long piece of writing.

Just tap once in that moment.

The grains you save collect in a bottle.

Bottles go into wooden crates.
Crates go into containers.
The time you have accumulated eventually becomes a vast warehouse.

When you look back at that warehouse, you may realise:

I thought I had done nothing,
but I lived through all of these days.

It is a place for keeping those memories.

In Hitotsubu, grains cannot be edited or deleted.

Even an accidental tap remains as one grain from that day.

This is not an app for creating a perfect record.
It is an app for preserving the time you actually lived, exactly as it happened.

You do not have to change your life.
You do not have to become positive.

Just remember:

Something tasted a little better.
I smiled a little.
Something helped me.
I made it through today.

Do not let those moments disappear.

One grain may not change anything.

But someday, that grain may remind you that something was still alive within you.
apps.name: Hitotsubu

apps.description:
Would you wait 14 days to save $20?

Buy or Wait Calculator is not a price predictor. It does not guess whether a sale is coming or tell you what a product will cost next week.

Instead, you enter today's price, the price you would be happy to pay, and how long you are willing to wait. The app makes the tradeoff between money and time visible.

Use it for planned purchases where timing matters as much as price.

Price trackers tell you what changed. Buy or Wait helps you decide whether the savings are worth the waiting for you.
apps.name: Buy or Wait Calculator

apps.description:
More helpful than a thick manual:
a simple “right here” from someone you know.

CuePic is an app for gently showing where to tap, where to look, or what to follow by adding marks to an image.

“Tap here.”
“Look here.”
“Follow these steps.”

“The button in the top right”, “the item below that”, “the blue part” —
words alone can be surprisingly hard to understand.

With CuePic, you can choose an image, add a red circle or rectangle, and share it right away.
Add a clear “right here” to the words you already know how to say.

When you want to help a family member with a phone.
When you want to show a friend where to look.
When you want someone at work to check a specific spot.

Start with one image and mark it with a red circle or rectangle.
For someone you do not want to confuse, add a pointer or arrow to make it even clearer.
For steps you do not want to explain over and over, you can turn multiple images into a simple guide.

When explaining gets a little easier,
the conversation can feel a little kinder.

CuePic is a small image explanation app that helps reduce misunderstandings and deliver a simple “right here.”

Main features:

・Add red circles or rectangles to images
・Clearly show where to tap or where to look
・Share the image you made right away
・Use pointers and arrows to make things stand out
・Combine multiple images into step-by-step instructions
・Helpful for explaining phone steps to family
・Useful for work checks and quick guidance for friends

Use CuePic when:

・You want to show someone where to tap on their phone
・You want to point out where to look in an image
・Words alone are hard to explain
・You want to say “right here” with one image
・You want to show multiple screens as steps
・You want to make explanation a little easier

CuePic delivers a “right here” that is a little kinder for both the person explaining and the person receiving it.
apps.name: CuePic

apps.description:
Work. Housework. Sleep. Then the same day begins again.

There was a time when I thought this might continue forever.

One night, I stayed up late throwing darts by myself.

It was not productive.
It did not immediately change my future.

But that time had not been assigned to me by anyone else. It was time I had chosen for myself.

Kizami is an app for digging out and keeping the time you chose from within everyday life.

The time you spent reading.
The time you walked a little farther.
The time you ate something you loved.
The time you did nothing and rested.
The time you became absorbed in something on your own.

It does not have to be impressive.
It does not have to be useful for your future.

If you chose it, it was your time.

The time you record accumulates as a single mine shaft extending underground.

As you dig deeper, your depth is compared with buildings, mountains, ocean depths, the Earth, and distances through space.

Kizami has no streaks to maintain and no system that judges whether you achieved a goal.

It is all right to miss a day.
It is all right if the time was short.

There was a moment in your day that you chose for yourself.

Kizami is a place to keep those moments, one by one.

Kizami is a small app created and maintained by one independent developer.

If it becomes meaningful to you, I would be grateful if you supported it with a review.
Your words give me the strength to keep building it.
apps.name: Kizami

apps.description:
You had five minutes.
You had things to do.
But the five minutes disappeared while you were deciding what to start.

Then another small pocket of time came, and choosing still took longer than starting. It was not because there was nothing to do. There was too much to choose from.

I used to be there too.

That is why I made Minpick—not to make you work harder, but to shorten the part where you have to decide.

Save something you want to do later and roughly how many minutes it takes. When you have 3 minutes, choose 3. When you have 5, choose 5. When you have 10, choose 10. Minpick shows up to three tasks that should fit.

You do not have to scan a long to-do list again. If you want to narrow things down, use category or priority—for example, only work, or only tasks with medium or high priority.

You can choose a time from the Home Screen widget. If a nudge helps, set a reminder for a day and time. You can switch languages in the app, and VoiceOver and Dynamic Type are supported.

If you want to stop, stop. If today is a day to rest, rest. You do not have to turn every spare minute into output, and you do not have to open Minpick every time.

Next time a few minutes open up and you have things to do but cannot decide what to start, open Minpick then.

I did not make it to push you harder. I made it to make that deciding moment a little shorter.

You still choose.

No account is required. Your saved tasks stay on your device. There are no adverts, subscriptions, or in-app purchases.
apps.name: Minpick

apps.description:
Milk, eggs, bread, water — some groceries come back every trip.

Repeat Grocery List is built for that one repetitive job: stop rebuilding the same shopping list over and over.

Add your usual items once. Check them off while you shop. When the trip is done, reset the same list and use it again next time.

There is no recipe planner, meal calendar, family feed, or complicated setup required.

One familiar list. Shop it, reset it, and use it again.
apps.name: Repeat Grocery List

apps.description: Before paying for a repair, check the warranty period. Enter the purchase date and warranty length to see the expected expiry date and time remaining. Track multiple products and choose reminder days and notification time for each one. Actual cover depends on the manufacturer's or seller's terms. Reminders need notification permission.
apps.name: Warranty Deadline Tracker

apps.description:
You finally have an evening to yourself. You only wanted to buy something you have been looking forward to. But here you are, switching between individual prices and bundle offers, opening the calculator again. Some items in the bundle are already yours. The minutes you hoped to enjoy are disappearing into another comparison. Eventually the comparisons feel like too much, so you just buy it. For a moment, the decision is over. Later you open your library, notice how your purchases overlap with things you already owned, and the regret returns.

I have done that too: bought something just to end the decision, then looked at my library and wished I had checked. I did not need another promise that something was “cheaper.” I needed to understand why a buying plan made sense.

With Bundlevero, enter the items you want, the ones you already own, individual prices, and bundle conditions. Compare purchase plans using fixed-price bundles, complete-the-set discounts, and must-buy-together offers. Paste a list or use on-device text recognition to help enter products.

Results use the prices and conditions you provide; there is no live price lookup. Check recognized names and prices against the source image. Complex cases may reach a search limit without a proven cheapest plan. Supports up to 20 items.

Bundlevero cannot undo a purchase or promise a life without regret. But before you press Buy out of sheer exhaustion again, give yourself one chance to check the cost and the reasoning. Let your library be a place for the things you wanted, not a reminder of another rushed choice.
apps.name: Bundlevero

apps.description:
How much of a discount would make a purchase worth it to you?

Enter the regular price and what you would actually pay. Buy Price Calculator works backward to show the discount percentage needed to reach your target.

Example: A regular price of 120 and a target of 90 means you need 25% off.

Save comparisons and revisit them when a sale appears. You can also account for tax and explore stacked discounts.

This app does not track stores, monitor prices, predict sales, or send price-drop alerts. You set the buying threshold; the app does the math.
apps.name: Buy Price Calculator

apps.description:
App Preview MP4 is a focused macOS utility for preparing App Store app preview videos.

Import a MOV or MP4 recording, choose the start and end points, check the selected range, choose an output size and create an MP4 that is ready to upload.

The app helps keep preview videos within the required 15 to 30 second duration. If a video is too short, the last image can be held for up to 15 seconds. If a video is too long, it can be shortened to 30 seconds.

Prepared output sizes make it easier to create preview videos for iPhone and iPad in portrait or landscape orientation. Custom sizes are also available when you need direct control.

Recordings can be imported with the file picker or by drag and drop. The app can also save copies of original files from Simulator or other temporary drag sources.

It is designed for developers who already have a Simulator, QuickTime or screen recording and want to reduce video upload errors in App Store Connect.

All processing happens locally on your Mac. No account, server, cloud upload, analytics or AI service is required.
apps.name: ClipPorter

apps.description:
Are you really a good person?

Good Person Test is a short personality test that reveals your “good person type” through 10 choices.

Each question gives you 3 options.
Once you choose, you cannot go back.

Do you help the person in front of you?
Do you follow the rules?
Do you smooth things over?
Or do you fix the system itself?

Your choices lead to one of 20 possible types, such as:

“Just-This-Once Angel”
“Kindness Debt Machine”
“Fairness Crusher”
“Goodwill Inc. CEO”

The types you discover are saved,
and you can review them anytime from the button in the top right.

The choice you make as a “good person”
may not always help everyone.

A little funny.
A little sharp.
A test app that measures how much you act like a good person.
apps.name: Good Person Test

apps.description:
What you want to create is already in your head.

You can see the part that needs fixing.
You know what you want to change.

Yet your work stops just because you have to explain to AI what “here” means.

Crop the image.
Save it.
Find where it was saved.
Wait for iCloud.
Move the file into a folder.
Drag it across.

Then turn something obvious at a glance into words:
“A little lower and to the left”
“Not the button, the empty space beneath it”

And still the result is:

“Not there”

Explain it again.
Wait again.
Check again.

You wanted AI to help you move faster, but tiny tasks needed only to point at one place keep breaking your train of thought.

You are not losing only a few seconds.
You are losing your focus.
Your creative momentum.
The next idea that was just in your head.
The feeling that you were moving forward.

What you really want is not to manage image files or write the perfect description of a location.

You want to turn an idea into something real before the spark fades.
You want to keep creating without stopping.
You want to end the day with something you made, not a pile of explanations.

Herebit removes the image busywork still standing between you and AI.

Choose an image.
Tap the place you want to point out.
That is all.

Then simply say:
“Fix this”
“Remove this”
“Make this space wider”

No cropping.
No hunting for saved files.
No moving files between folders.
No long explanations of where something is.

You no longer have to be AI’s image assistant.
You no longer have to search for the perfect wording.
You no longer have to repeat “not there” again and again.

You do not want a better explanation.
You want to be understood the first time.
You want to keep moving without breaking your train of thought.
You want to turn what is in your head into something real, one idea after another.

Herebit does not just give back the seconds lost to image handling.

It gives back your focus and creative speed.

Key features
• Choose an image and tap the place
• Show AI visually where a change is needed
• Share the marked image straight away
• No complicated editing tools
• Fewer explanations, mistakes and repeated attempts

Herebit is for you if you:
• Build apps or websites with AI
• Repeatedly edit specific parts of AI-generated images
• Want to point out buttons, text or empty space quickly
• Are tired of describing places that have no name
• Do not want tiny tasks to destroy your focus
• Want to turn ideas into reality without stopping

Do not cast a spell. Just point.

Do not waste time explaining.
Make what you want to make.
apps.name: Herebit

apps.description:
One product can look cheaper on the shelf and still cost more once you account for what you will not use.

Nokarvo compares two products by usable quantity, not just package quantity. Enter price and amount, then choose the level of detail that fits the situation: use the whole purchase, make a rough estimate, enter a measured usable amount, or subtract specific losses such as peel, shell, core, bone, trim, drained liquid, packaging, spoilage, and other unused portions.

When the shelf-price winner changes after those adjustments, Nokarvo shows the flip clearly.

What Nokarvo can show:
• Shelf price vs usable price
• Value not used
• Relative savings
• Rough, measured, or breakdown-based usable amounts
• Specific losses such as peel, bone, packaging, liquid, and spoilage
• A calculation receipt so you can see how the result was produced
• “Too close to call” when estimate ranges overlap instead of forcing a winner
• Mass, volume, and count comparisons
• Offline use with no account and no tracking

Useful for groceries, ingredients, produce, meat, seafood, bulk packs, household products, and any purchase where the amount you buy is not always the amount you actually use.

Nokarvo does not convert currencies or fetch product data from the internet. It has one job: help you compare the value of what you can actually use.
apps.name: Nokarvo

apps.description:
Buying items sold in packs? Work out how many you really need.

Enter the quantity required and the amount per pack. PackPlanner calculates the whole packs to buy, the total quantity purchased and what remains. For example, 2.5 kg in 700 g packs means 4 packs with 300 g left over.

Use weight, volume, length or item count. Compatible units are converted, and a breakdown explains the result.

Optionally enter a pack price for an estimated total. Name, save, search, edit and reuse plans, or copy the results.

Choose your app language, numeral style and displayed currency independently. Changing the currency does not perform exchange-rate conversion. No account is needed; your plans are stored on your device.
apps.name: Pack Quantity Calculator

apps.description:
Palette Spin is a simple wallpaper maker for turning colours, photos and text into custom iPhone wallpapers.

Start with a palette, spin through colour patterns and preview how your wallpaper looks on an iPhone-style screen. You can add a photo, adjust blend effects, place text, tune colours and save the result to Photos.

Palette Spin is designed for quick visual experiments:
・Spin palettes and colour patterns
・Create colourful gradient wallpapers
・Add photos as a background layer
・Adjust blend mode, opacity, scale and position
・Add text with custom font, colour, outline, shadow and rotation
・Preview portrait and landscape wallpaper layouts
・Save full wallpapers or split designs into tiles

Whether you want a bright Lock Screen, a soft gradient background or a personal wallpaper with text and photos, Palette Spin helps you make it quickly.
apps.name: Palette Spin

apps.description:
Bacchus Karma is a block puzzle where you can build the board and decide how pieces appear.

Choose which pieces can appear, set the board's starting layout, and adjust how likely each piece is to show up.

During play, you have up to 30 seconds for each move.
Drag the piece and decide where to place it.

Build the board.
Choose how pieces appear.
Then play under the rules you created.

Simple controls let you make and play your own falling-block puzzle.
apps.name: Bacchus Karma

apps.description:
I was in Japan, building apps on my own.

I didn't know anyone in Saudi Arabia.

Someone in Saudi Arabia found an app I had made by myself in Japan.

Someone introduced it in Arabic.

But what truly made me happy wasn't simply that someone had introduced the app.

They didn't just follow the way I had imagined presenting it.

They chose the screenshots themselves.

They explained in their own words what kind of app it was.

They decided for themselves what needed to be shown so people would understand it.

And somehow, their explanation was clearer than mine.

It was my app, but when I saw the way they presented it,

“So this is how you show it so people understand.”

I was the one who learned something.

## Then, through that connection, a different person asked for “an app that remembers”

A different person in Saudi Arabia sent me a DM in English.

Car service.
Parts replacement.
Fuel.
Insurance.

They asked if I could make an app for things like that.

I wrote back honestly:

> I don't know cars very well

Then I asked:

**What are you struggling with most right now?**

Then one phrase came back.

> App you can remember about your car

**An app that can remember things about your car.**

Then IkmahLog could remember those things.

You don't have to keep everything in your head.
When you need it, just look at IkmahLog.

Maintenance, for example, every three months.

By mileage, 5,000 km.
10,000 km.

The English messages from there became Swift variables here.
They became screens.
They became conditional branches in the code.

# The incident

## “Where is the fuel record?”

They actually used it through TestFlight.

**Where is the fuel record?**

**It was genuinely missing from the Maintenance screen.**

I had looked at the screens.
I had written the code.
I had made the build.

And yet I had missed it.

The person in Saudi Arabia found it because they actually used the app.

In reality, **they were also finding things I couldn't see and helping IkmahLog.**

Ask.
Build.
Let someone use it.
Get something wrong.
Fix it.
Send it again.

**Because the other person actually used the app, the code changed.**

## I began to see one person's life

Three months.
5,000 km.
10,000 km.
95-octane gasoline.
Insurance renewal.
Arabic.
TestFlight.
One sentence: “Where is Fuel?”

In a place that had once been only on the far side of a map, I began to see one person's life.

## Before IkmahLog and after IkmahLog

One change belongs to the person using it.

### Before

**I have to remember all of this myself.**

### After

**When I need it, I can just look at IkmahLog.**

But there is another Before / After.

This one belongs to me, the person who made the app.

### Before

I had begun to see that there were real people behind the name “Saudi Arabia.”

But I still didn't know how this person lived.

### After

IkmahLog now contains **things that would never have been there if I had built it entirely on my own.**

And maybe, after IkmahLog, **I'm no longer the same kind of maker I was before.**
Main features
• Garage for managing multiple vehicles
• Maintenance, parts, fuel, and insurance records
• Date, mileage, cost, quantity, notes, photos, and file attachments
• Set what comes next by date and/or mileage
• Repeating reminders and local notifications
• iCloud sync
• ZIP backup and restore
• In-app switching across 50 languages

IkmahLog does not diagnose your vehicle or decide manufacturer maintenance schedules for you. You decide.

It started with one person's

**“I want an app that can remember things about my car.”**

That was the HELP.

While I was building it, I was helped too.

I think IkmahLog is still continuing that story.
apps.name: IkmahLog: Vehicle Records

apps.description:
Pudding is a simple mini game where you scoop pudding little by little with a drag gesture.

The rules are easy.
Keep scooping to raise your score, then pull back before the caramel appears.

Maybe you can go a little further.
But the next scoop might end it.

Enjoy that small push-your-luck moment in short, quick sessions.

Aim for a new high score, or play it like a tiny daily test of luck.
There are no complicated controls, so it is easy to play during a short break.

You can also check your play history and try to beat your past records.

Ads have been removed so the flow of play is easier to enjoy.
If you like the app, you can support development through the coffee item.
apps.name: PuddingScoop

apps.description:
After being in a crowd,
there are days when you cannot do anything.

Sometimes a run of notifications is enough
to scatter everything in your head.

A sudden change of plans,
or a slightly harsh tone,
can wear you down more than you expected.

But in the moment, it is hard to explain.
You are not trying to make it a big deal.
You simply end up unable to move later.

Quiet Reserve is an app for briefly recording
those days when small stimuli wear you down easily.

You do not need to write a long diary.
Crowds, notifications, plan changes, tone of voice, sounds, waiting for a reply.
Choose what feels close,
then record how much you have left right now, like a water level.

As your records grow,
you can quietly look back at
which stimuli tend to wear you down,
and which ways of coping left you with a little energy.

Quiet Reserve does not diagnose you.
It does not ask you to improve.
You do not need to use it every day.

It does not call you “too sensitive”.
It does not say you are “overthinking”.
It simply keeps a record of how that day wore you down.

For people who cannot do anything after being in a crowd.

Quiet Reserve is a quiet recording app
for people who get tired easily from stimuli.

Main features:
・record what wore you down with tags
・record your current reserve like a water level
・add what you did to cope only when needed
・review recent records
・mode for recording only the level
・silent mode with no sounds
・with Quiet Reserve+, use search, period review, export, and theme changes

Even on the free version, you can keep recording.
Use Quiet Reserve+ only when you want to organise your records more.
apps.name: Quiet Reserve

apps.description: Don't remember a return only after the window closes. Enter a purchase date and return period to see the deadline and days left. Save multiple items and choose reminder days and notification time for each one. Return conditions vary by retailer; check the store's policy. Reminders need notification permission.
apps.name: Return Deadline Tracker

apps.description:
Breathe at your own rhythm.

Soft Count is a breathing app you can shape around yourself — from session length and breathing rhythm to visuals and haptics.

Whether you want a one-minute reset or a longer, slower session, choose the rhythm that fits the moment: Natural, Relaxation, Zen, Resonant, or Calming.

• Start right from a Home Screen widget with your preferred time and breathing rhythm
• Choose 1, 3, 5, or 10 minutes
• Change breathing rhythms during a session without losing your remaining time or progress
• Use Focus Studio to adjust rings, markers, display layers, glow, thickness, size, rotation, and more in real time
• Follow inhale, hold, exhale, and other breathing phases through haptic guidance
• Set daily breathing reminders
• Choose System, Light, or Dark appearance
• Switch the app language from inside Soft Count, including support for right-to-left languages

Soft Count is not here to force you into one prescribed way of breathing.
It gives you the freedom to choose the breathing experience that feels right for you.
apps.name: Soft Count

apps.description:
Stockout Zero is a simple incremental inventory management game about turning tiny stock checks into unstoppable automation.

Tap to check stock, earn money, buy upgrades, and build systems that bring you closer to zero stockouts.

At first, it is just a small shop task.
Soon, it becomes a full inventory operation.

Features:
- Simple tap-based gameplay
- Upgrade-based progression
- Automation systems
- Fast clear leaderboards with Game Center
- Daily, weekly, and all-time ranking challenges

How fast can you reach Stockout Zero?
apps.name: Stockout Zero

apps.description:
After a cancellation notice,
the empty time keeps getting closer
while you are still wondering who to contact.

You do not want to send a mass message.
You do not want to lower your price.
But if you do nothing, today’s income disappears.

That is not a problem with your judgment.
You did not want to treat clients carelessly, lower the value of your work, or give up today’s open slot.
You were trying to protect all of them at once.

TwelveOath is an app that helps you prepare, before the next cancellation happens:
the next person to contact,
the reason to contact them,
and the deadline for waiting for a reply.

When a cancellation happens, contact one person.
Wait for their reply.
If it does not work, move to the next person.
If needed, switch to a public notice.

Do not let your only choices be a mass message, a discount, or doing nothing.

TwelveOath helps you avoid repeating the same 30 minutes again.
apps.name: TwelveOath

apps.description:
Unit Choice is a price comparison app that helps you compare the unit price of each product by simply entering the price and quantity.

Even when products have different sizes, quantities or pack formats, you can check the unit price, cheapest option, average and median in one place.

“The price looks low, but is it really good value?”
“Should I choose the larger pack or the smaller one?”
“Is this more expensive or cheaper than what I bought before?”

Unit Choice was created to reduce those doubts while shopping and help you choose with more confidence.

You can save the details you enter in a list, review them later and compare the same products again whenever needed.

Recommended for anyone who does not want to miss differences in price, quantity or pack size during everyday shopping.
apps.name: Unit Choice

apps.description:
"I'm never smoking again."

I made that decision and threw away the cigarettes I had.

But determination alone does not change a person.

You decide not to smoke, then smoke again.
You decide to change, then return to the same day.

What you lose each time is not only your health or your money.

The feeling that you cannot even keep a promise you made to yourself begins to remain inside you.

If you keep telling yourself that you will change tomorrow, tomorrow will probably be the same.

So I stopped trying to solve a lifetime of not smoking.

First, move the next cigarette out of reach.
Prepare something else to do when the urge comes.
Face the life you do not want to return to and what you want to regain.

Then get through only the first 72 hours.

BreakThree turns what I actually did to get through those first three days into one guided sequence.

This app will not turn you into a different person.

But it will show you, one step at a time, what you can do right now to avoid the next cigarette.

Once you begin, three candles and the remaining time quietly show your progress through the 72 hours.

When the urge to smoke appears, open the 30-second breathing screen and pause.

Main features

• Progress through the first 72 hours after quitting
• Preparation to move the next cigarette out of reach
• Alternative actions you can prepare in advance
• Reminders of the life you do not want to return to
• Reminders of what you want to regain
• A 30-second support screen for cravings
• Small and medium widgets
• A three-day record stored on your device

Not tomorrow. Start with the next cigarette.

Not forever. Start with 72 hours.

BreakThree is not a substitute for medical care or treatment. If you experience severe withdrawal symptoms or feel unwell, contact a qualified healthcare professional or smoking-cessation service.
apps.name: BreakThree

apps.description:
JiiyaRoll is a casual idle game where you roll dice, collect funds, and hire quirky staff to grow your team.

The controls are simple. Roll the dice to collect funds, add staff members, improve efficiency, and keep building your team step by step.

As the game progresses, various events may appear. Make choices based on the situation and continue strengthening your team.

It is easy to play in short sessions while still offering a steady sense of progress.

This app does not include real-money gambling, betting, cash-out, prizes, or wagering.
apps.name: Jiiya Roll

apps.description:
Do you have to decide again today?

Since this morning, you’ve already chosen, thought things through, considered everyone else, and made one decision after another.
When the day is finally nearly over, one last question remains:
what are we eating today?

The truth is, you don’t want to think about it anymore.
But if you ask someone else, the answer is often, “I don’t mind.”
Suggest something, and you might hear, “Not that.”
And if you’re on your own, you end up choosing the same familiar thing again.

Time passes without a decision.
Then you open an expensive food delivery app because you’re too tired to keep thinking.
You forget there’s already food in the fridge.
You forget the restaurant you wanted to try and the meal you meant to cook.

And in the end, you eat the same thing again.

Once or twice, it doesn’t seem like a problem.
But when it happens every day, a quiet feeling begins to build:
you’re no longer choosing how you live — your exhaustion is choosing for you.

You spend more.
Food goes to waste.
You keep eating the same things.
The question “What should we eat?” starts to wear you down.
And then you feel a little frustrated with yourself for being unable to make such a simple decision.

It isn’t because you’re indecisive.
Perhaps you’ve simply made too many decisions already today.

So at least this final one can be let go.

MealDrift chooses one meal for today from the options you saved while you still had more energy, helping the tired version of you at the end of the day.

You don’t have to give up your own tastes.
And you don’t have to leave everything to pure chance.

Save the meals you love, restaurants you visit often, food you cook at home, leftovers, and anything you would genuinely be happy to eat.
Then let the app choose one of them for today.

You don’t make the decision yourself.
But the result still feels like yours.

No more:
“Fine, let’s just have this.”

Instead:
“Yes, this is what we’re having today.”

You don’t have to be the only person making the decision every night.
You don’t have to order a takeaway simply because you couldn’t choose.
You don’t have to forget what’s in the fridge and throw it away later.
You don’t have to blame yourself for choosing the same thing again.

You aren’t setting up MealDrift only for who you are today.
You’re leaving options for tomorrow’s version of you, when there’s no energy left to think.

MealDrift is a small safety net for your meals, left for your tired future self.

You no longer have to spend your last bit of energy deciding what to eat today.

Key features

• Chooses one meal for today from your saved options
• Sets how often each option appears using three simple levels
• Sets suitable months and seasons
• Filters or excludes options using tags
• Hides an option for today or for a set period
• Records the date, taste, portion size and whether you want it again
• Searches your history by meal name or tag
• Backs up and transfers data using JSON
• No account required
• Your data is never sent to a server

The options you left behind when you still had energy will return to help when you’re tired.

With MealDrift, let go of the last decision of your day.
apps.name: MealDrift
